items.markdown:
**Construction Capital** is `a London-based property finance brokerage founded by Matt Lenzie that arranges senior debt, mezzanine finance, and equity for UK property developers` . The term can also refer more broadly to working capital and funding solutions used in the building industry to manage cash flow.[](https://constructioncapital.co.uk/) [[1]](https://constructioncapital.co.uk/)[[2]](https://constructioncapital.co.uk/about)[[3]](https://greenwoodcapital.co.uk/resources/what-is-construction-finance/)Financial Services & Brokerage

- **Property Development Finance:** Securing funding packages from a large panel of lenders for residential and commercial schemes.
- **Debt and Equity Options:** Structuring senior debt, mezzanine layers, joint ventures, and equity partnerships.
- **Industry Focus:** Tailoring financial structures around standard construction payment methods like application stages and retention clauses.[](https://constructioncapital.co.uk/) [[1]](https://constructioncapital.co.uk/locations/greater-london)

Working Capital in Construction

- **Cash Flow Management:** Bridging the gap between paying for labor/materials and receiving certified client payments.
- **Invoice Financing:** Unlocking capital tied up in unpaid or pending applications for payment.[](https://octagoncapital.co.uk/construction-finance/) [[1]](https://octagoncapital.co.uk/construction-finance/)

If you are looking for specific information, please let me know if you need:

- Details on **arranging development finance** through Construction Capital
- General information on **construction working capital loans** 
- Information for a different **company or region**

items.title: What is the formula for working capital for contractors?

expanded_element.title: A Contractor's Guide to Working Capital - Procore
expanded_element.description:
Working Capital = Current Assets – Current Liabilities
 Thus, calculating working capital allows a contractor to determine whether they have access to sufficient cash to pay bills in the near term. The formula only looks at “current” assets and liabilities because these are short-term measures.
